## 11.2 ⭐ THE ANALYSIS MODEL — B8. Frozen before any decoder output exists.

⛔ **The previous draft contained NO analysis model.** The word *bootstrap*
appeared once, inside a rule constraining a method that was never specified:
no interval procedure, no resampling unit assigned to any estimand, no resample
count, no seed, no multiplicity handling. **§2 promises "each with its
uncertainty" and nothing said how.** That left the unit choosable after the data
existed, which is the largest free parameter a study can carry.

### 11.2.1 The experimental unit is the RECORDING

| level | what it is | n |
|---|---|---|
| **cell** | one (recording × arm × condition × metric) measurement | — |
| ⭐ **recording** | **THE EXPERIMENTAL UNIT.** One performance of one text, by one speaker, in one state. | Set S 1 302 · Set L see §3.3 |
| text | one script line. 31 texts in Set S; Set L's text count is declared in `GATE4_CORPUS.json`. | 31 (+ Set L) |
| speaker | 7 | 7 |
| state | 6 (Set S) · 2 (Set L) | 6 / 2 |

⛔ **CELLS ARE NOT INDEPENDENT OBSERVATIONS AND ARE NEVER TREATED AS SUCH.** The
duration-ladder cells are **repeated measures on Set L recordings already
counted**. Resampling cells would count those performances several times each
and narrow every interval by a factor nobody declared.

### 11.2.2 Interval procedure

> **CLUSTER BOOTSTRAP over RECORDINGS, resampled with replacement.**
> **`n_resamples = 4000`. `seed = 20260911`** — the one study seed, matching
> E1's frozen choice so Gate 3 and Gate 4 intervals are produced the same way.
> **Percentile interval at 95%.** The point estimate is the **median** (§13:
> descriptive as primary).

**One recording is one draw, and every cell belonging to it travels with it.**
A recording that carries five ladder cells contributes all five or none.

**Paired estimands (Q3 the controlled pair, Q7 the Mimi ablation) resample the
recording ONCE and take both arms' values from that draw**, so the pairing is
preserved inside every resample. This is the same paired-median-bootstrap
construction Gate 3 used for E1.

### 11.2.3 Aggregation hierarchy — declared per estimand, never chosen later

```
cell -> recording -> (speaker x state) -> arm
```

**Each estimand names its resampling unit and its aggregation path in its own
row of the output.** Where an estimand pools across states or speakers, it
aggregates **within (speaker × state) first, then across**, so a speaker with
more admissible recordings cannot dominate a pooled figure.

| estimand | resampling unit | aggregated over |
|---|---|---|
| Q0 · Q1 · Q2 · Q3 · Q7 · Q9 | recording | (speaker × state) → arm |
| ⛔ Q5 · Q6 — **NOT YET ADMISSIBLE, METRIC NOT BUILT / NOT FUZZED (D10)** | recording *(when built)* | *(when built)* |
| Q4 duration dependence | **recording** (ladder cells are repeated measures) | rung → arm |
| ⛔ Q8 drift — **DEPENDS ON Q5, NOT YET ADMISSIBLE (D10)** | **passage** (windows are repeated measures within it) | passage → arm |

### 11.2.4 Multiplicity — declared families, and no significance claims

**Gate 4 reports intervals and effect sizes. It performs NO hypothesis tests, so
there is no p-value to correct** (§13: "no multiplicity correction unless a
declared family needs one"; families are declared before anything is computed).

The declared families:

| family | members |
|---|---|
| F1 route-A round-trip fidelity | Route A arms × the ranking metrics |
| F2 route-B analysis–resynthesis fidelity | Route B arms × the ranking metrics |
| F3 streaming cost within arm | arms with an achievable E3 |
| F4 controlled pair | the E1 pair alone |
| F5 depth ablation | `mimi_q8` vs `mimi_q32` alone |

⛔ **Families are never merged, and Route A and Route B never share one.**

⚠️ **Interval multiplicity is DECLARED, not corrected.** With many arms and
several metrics, some intervals will exclude zero by chance. **No claim rests on
a single interval excluding zero.** §11.1's six conditions govern every ranking
claim, and condition 5's floor is the `rate_chain_floor` of §11.2.5 — a
magnitude threshold, not a significance threshold.

### 11.2.5 ⭐ THE RANKING RULE — rewritten for D2

⛔ **`rate_chain_floor` CANNOT license a ranking, and the reason is structural.**
The null route is `master → sr_in → sr_out`; **15 of 18 arms have
`sr_in == sr_out`**, so that route is byte-identical to the reference and the
floor is **exactly 0.0**. MEASURED for every real arm chain:

| arms | chain | floor (native) | floor (common 16 k) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 causal FocalCodec | 16 000 → 24 000 | 70.79 | 28.39 |
| **the other 15** | `sr_in == sr_out` | **0.0** | **0.0** |

A control at 16 000 → 44 100 — which no arm has — returns 53.87, so the function
works and **zero is the structural result, not a bug.** B4 moved the condition
from *unsatisfiable* to *unfailable*. `rate_chain_floor` is retained as a
**reported diagnostic** for the three arms where it is non-zero, and licenses
nothing.

### ⭐ What licenses a ranking instead — two conditions, both preregistered

**(a) UNCERTAINTY.** The paired effect between two arms with a **95%
recording-cluster bootstrap interval** (§11.2.2: 4 000 resamples, seed
20260911, recordings resampled with replacement, ladder cells travelling with
their recording). **The interval must exclude zero.**

**(b) THE MEASURED, STATE-AWARE INSTRUMENT FLOOR.**

⛔ **B2 — THE SINGLE-DRAW FLOOR IS WITHDRAWN AND IS NOT A LIVE RULE ANYWHERE.**
This section previously defined the floor as **9.09% of a rung, `mcd` ≈ 23.88**,
while §6.1.2 and §11.1 had already withdrawn it. **That is roughly 4× too low —
the exact error F2 was raised to fix — and this is the section Stage 2
implements.** Its old explanatory sentence ("the difference between those two
numbers is the floor") described a construction that is not how the floor is
computed. **Both are struck. The value 23.88 survives ONLY as withdrawn
historical evidence in §6.1.2.**

> ⭐ **THE AUTHORITATIVE FLOORS — state-specific, in ABSOLUTE `mcd`, from
> `fuzz_gate4_lib.json` → `INSTRUMENT_FLOORS.mcd.per_state`:**

| state | mildest rung | floor (fraction) | **floor — ABSOLUTE `mcd`** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Neutral | 257.6 | 0.3691 | **95.08** |
| Angry | 144.6 | 0.4660 | **67.39** |
| Happy | 240.1 | 0.3416 | **81.99** |
| Scared | 146.7 | 0.7163 | **105.07** |
| Shouting | 255.2 | 0.3154 | **80.51** |
| Whisper | 86.7 | 0.9753 | **84.59** |

⭐ **M1 — RANKING COMPARISONS AND FLOORS ARE EVALUATED IN ABSOLUTE `mcd` UNITS.**

> **A single-state comparison uses THAT state's absolute floor.**
>
> **A POOLED comparison uses the MAXIMUM ABSOLUTE FLOOR over every contributing
> state** — **not** the largest fraction.

⛔ **The previous rule named the worst FRACTION (Whisper, 0.9753) and was on the
wrong scale.** An `mcd` effect is an absolute quantity, and the fraction form is
undefined for a pooled set because the rung is per state and per calibration
recording. **MEASURED: Whisper's fraction is the largest (0.9753) but its
absolute floor is 84.59, while Scared's is 105.07.** A pooled comparison
spanning both would have been held to 84.59 where Scared alone requires
105.07 — **under-protecting by 24.2%.**

> **Pooled floor over all six states = 105.07 absolute `mcd` (Scared).**

**(c) ⭐ B1 — THE VALIDATED-SUPPORT DOMAIN.** Before either condition is
evaluated, **each cell must lie inside the region where `mcd`'s ranking property
was validated** (§6.1.3). A cell outside it is
**`NOT COMPARABLE — OUTSIDE VALIDATED SUPPORT`** and receives no `mcd` ranking.

⛔ **NO PRACTICAL-EFFECT OR PERCEPTUAL THRESHOLD IS DECLARED, because none is
defensible before the perception phase exists.** Gate 4 therefore may **order**
arms by a ranking metric with its interval attached, and **may not** claim that
an ordering is *meaningful*, *audible*, *important* or *sufficient to choose an
architecture*.

> **Where (a) or (b) fails, the output says `ORDERED, SEPARATION NOT
> ESTABLISHED`** and displays the interval. That is a first-class state, not a
> blank.

⛔ **A ranking is never inferred from an aggregate, never from a single interval
excluding zero (§11.2.4), and never across routes.**

## 12. Execution plan — two stages, so the metric never touches the arm's environment

**⛔ Nothing in this section runs until this document is approved and the corpus
is chosen.**

### Stage 1 — decode and persist (one process per environment, strictly sequential)

Runs in `decbench`, `decbench_melflow` and — read-only — `fish`. §7.4 applies:
**one GPU process at a time.** §7.3 machine-state discipline applies and is
recorded per cell.

For each (arm, utterance): encode once → hash the representation → decode
offline → decode streamed at the arm's E3 condition (where one exists) → run the
§7.2 determinism probe → write **float32 WAV** for every produced signal → record
the §8 verdict, the sha256 of every WAV, and the full environment header.

⭐ **Every produced waveform is persisted.** Metrics are recomputable from disk
without re-running a decode, and a later metric repair never requires re-running
the GPU stage. *(This closes a named weakness: not persisting per-observation raw
data.)*

### Stage 2 — metrics (one process, one environment, CPU/GPU, no arm imports)

Reads WAVs and the corpus manifest. Computes tiers A/B/C. **Nothing in Stage 2
imports a codec.** This keeps metric dependencies out of `fish` entirely and
means a metric can be fixed and rerun without touching a frozen decode.

**Order is fixed and is part of the pre-registration:**

```
1. gate4_corpus.py             → GATE4_CORPUS.json (selection + sha256)
                                 ⛔ D12: the fuzz calibrates on this file's
                                 HELD-OUT subset and exits without it, so the
                                 corpus MUST come first. The previous order
                                 listed the fuzz at step 1 and could not run.
2. gate4_source_gate.py        → source-only validity, all sets incl. calibration
3. fuzz_gate4_lib.py           → tiers, gates, INSTRUMENT FLOOR
                                 ⛔ BEFORE any real number
                                 (the deleted resampler-damage floor is NOT
                                 among its outputs — see §6.1.2)
4. Q0 the environment control  → gates fish
5. Stage 1 decode + persist
6. Stage 2 metrics
7. GATE4_MATRIX.md / gate4_matrix.json / results/gate4_*.csv
8. independent adversarial review          ⛔ before any number leaves the repo
9. freeze: freeze_gate4.py, hashes, verifier
```

### Artifacts Gate 4 will produce

```
GATE4_PREREG.md            this file, frozen
GATE4_PREREG_FROZEN.json   every pinned constant, model id, revision, threshold
GATE4_CORPUS.json          provenance, licence, per-file sha256, selection log
fuzz_gate4_lib.py / .json  the instrument fuzz, run first
gate4_lib.py               new metrics only; everything else imported
gate4_run.py               Stage 1
gate4_metrics.py           Stage 2
results/gate4_raw_*.jsonl  every observation, every failure, every state
results/gate4_wavs/        every persisted waveform, hashed
GATE4_MATRIX.md/.json      the authoritative matrix
GATE4_AUDIT.md             the independent review trail
freeze_gate4.py            hashes + --verify, extending the Gate 3 pattern
```

### Cost — ESTIMATE, not a measurement

19 arms × 1 736 cells (§3.3) × (offline + streamed) ≈ **~66 000 decodes**,
plus 12 long-form passages × 5 duration conditions. Decodes are millisecond-scale
per Gate 3, so **Stage 1 is dominated by model load/unload under block
randomisation, not by decoding**. Persisted audio: **~4–6 GB** at float32.
**Stage 2's ASR pass is the expensive term** — roughly 11 000 ASR runs; if that
proves impractical, Q6 runs on a **declared subset fixed before Stage 2 starts**
(the first 10 utterances per speaker by the §3.3 sort), never on a subset chosen
after seeing a result.

⚠️ **Every number in this cost block is an ESTIMATE derived from Gate 3's
measured decode times and typical file sizes. None of it is measured.**

## 13. What Gate 4 does NOT answer

1. **Perceptual quality.** No listening test. Which decoder *sounds* best is not measured and no sentence may imply it.
2. **End-to-end TTS quality.** The generator is outside this study.
3. **Cloning / voice-conversion quality.** Requires a generator.
4. **Production precision.** fp32 only. A candidate that wins at fp32 has not been shown to win at bf16/fp16.
5. **Noisy, reverberant, conversational, overlapped, sung or non-English audio.** Clean read speech only (§3.2).
6. **Generalisation beyond this machine.** One RTX 5080, one driver, one torch version.
7. **Whether a decoder could be trained better.** Published checkpoints, inference only.
8. **`nanocodec`.** BLOCKED — and that is a fact about NVIDIA's shipped Windows runtime path, **not** evidence that the architecture requires Linux and **not** evidence that a standalone Windows decoder could not be written.
9. **Batch > 1.**

⛔ **Gate 4 does not select the TTS architecture either.** It removes one of the
two gates §16.2 names. The end-to-end generator→decoder streaming study and the
production-precision gate both remain unrun, and the Phase-1 candidate-scope
limit stands: **without a deliberate survey, the winner of this study is the best
thing already installed on this machine.**

### What the reviewer is specifically asked to attack

1. **§3.0 — the ordering defect.** The source was declared *after* exploration. Is the recovery sound, or does the recomputed set still carry the original tree's fingerprint?
2. **§3.3 — the `[3.0 s, 10.0 s]` window**, which was widened from 2.0 s *after source durations had been read*. Instrument correction, or tuning?
3. **§6.2 — the two author process failures**, and whether the final fuzz rule is sound given that it changed during construction.
4. **§3.3 L6 — cells versus recordings.** Is the resampling unit correctly specified everywhere it is used?
5. **§9.1 — Q0 gating `fish`**, and whether a quality-comparability result may be granted while timing comparability stays refused.
6. **§11.1 — the six conditions for lifting `QUALITY COMPARISON NOT ESTABLISHED`.** Are they sufficient?
7. **The corrected §3.2 level claim.** An earlier draft asserted normalisation had flattened the state levels; measurement over 1 512 files refuted it. Is the corrected statement now within the evidence?

### ⭐ Added for the DELTA review, after the first adversarial round (B1–B10, M1–M11)

8. **§11.2.5 — the replacement floor.** `rate_chain_floor` is the arm's own rate chain with the codec removed. Is it the right null, and is it computable for every arm and both denominators?
9. **§5.3 B7 — envelope alignment.** Does an envelope gate admit a spectrally faithful, phase-incoherent reconstruction *and* still reject a genuinely misaligned one? The fuzz validates it on synthetic phase destruction with no decoder; is that validation sufficient?
10. **§6 G4 — the length gate.** Does a truncated estimate now fail rather than score as identity, for every metric?
11. **§11.2 — the analysis model.** Is the recording the right unit everywhere, and are the ladder cells correctly treated as repeated measures?
12. **§3.3 L2 — the derived rung.** It is now chosen mechanically as the largest candidate keeping 100% of Set L. Is the candidate ladder itself a hidden free parameter?
13. **§5.3 M2 — REFERENCE-NATIVE is now declared a WITHIN-ARM denominator only.** Does any surviving cross-arm claim still rest on it?
14. **§3.5.1 B2 — the denoise control is `NOT MEASURED`.** Is carrying that as an unquantified scope limit acceptable, or does it sink the whisper estimand?
